findings.claim: Endpoint-coordinate effects are dominated by shape (second-moment) descriptors rather than centroid translation: shape_yy shows the strongest integrated high-low contrast (z=-0.513, q=1.5e-5, 0/14 positive batches), with shape_xx (z=-0.495, q=8.1e-4) and shape_zz (z=-0.183, q=0.067) aligned in the same negative direction. Centroid components are weak or null (global_centroid_x z=-0.111, q=0.257; global_centroid_z z=-0.061, q=0.481), except global_centroid_y (z=-0.243, q=0.014).

The continuous contrast functions over the observed window are non-monotone and unstable: landmark_00_local_dy has 6 sign changes with first_rate_z=-72.4 and last_rate_z=+5.5; landmark_00_local_dx has 6 sign changes with first_rate_z=-17.5 and last_rate_z=+8.1; landmark_00_local_dz has 10 sign changes. Polynomial fits are not accepted and extrapolation is disallowed for all inspected features, so a constant rule is not supported and only observed-node interpolation is defensible.

Whole-window mean contrasts are near zero for the inspected landmark features (e.g. landmark_00_soft_mass whole_window_z=0.639, landmark_00_local_dy whole_window_z=-0.301, landmark_00_local_dz whole_window_z=-0.024), while first/last rate z-scores are large and opposite in sign. This indicates the endpoint-coordinate signal is a time-conditioned rate change rather than a stable level shift, and the contrast curve is not an absolute reward target.

The declared objective is final predicted target affinity primary with validity and strain secondary under coordinate-only control; the supplied observations are endpoint-coordinate contrast and trend diagnostics, not decoded terminal affinity labels, so no observed quantity here directly measures final affinity benefit.

hypotheses.falsifier: shape_yy/shape_xx integrated contrast loses sign or significance under multiplicity adjustment in an independent batch set
hypotheses.statement: Signed favorable-versus-comparison coordinate contrasts at observed selection nodes are concentrated in shape (second-moment) descriptors, so a time-conditioned rule keyed to shape_yy/shape_xx direction would differ from a constant centroid rule.

hypotheses.falsifier: constant rule matches or exceeds time-conditioned rule on held-out observed nodes
hypotheses.scope: observed score nodes only, no extrapolation
hypotheses.statement: Because local landmark contrast rates change sign within the observed window, a time-conditioned contrast rule should outperform a constant rule on the same observed nodes.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels or independent outcome data were supplied; last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.
Selection enrichment versus absolute geometric descriptors cannot be separated without the population/label binding beyond the delivered contrast tables.
Uncertainty/multiplicity-adjusted ranking versus point-estimate ranking could not be fully demonstrated because only a subset of the 200 continuous_trends and 74 endpoint_effects rows was read.
Joint-pattern versus marginal coupling diagnostics (joint_diagnostics, covariance) were not read in this turn, so coupling/redundancy claims are unsupported.
Turnover accounting and parent-child increment contrasts were not read, so within-path change versus cohort-composition change is unresolved.
